quarterly_data.signal: Q4 2025 total revenue was $136.4 million, up 8% from $126.5 million in the previous quarter and up 48% from $92.2 million in the fourth quarter of 2024; infrastructure revenue was approximately $47 million (up 76% in Q4 year-on-year and 30% for the full year), broadband approximately $58 million, connectivity approximately $18 million and industrial multimarket approximately $14 million; GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins were approximately 57.6% and 59.6%. CEO called 2025 'a clear inflection year' with 30% revenue growth and said the infrastructure category should emerge in 2026 as the single largest contributor to overall revenues. Q4 exit cash was approximately $101.4 million after repurchasing approximately $20 million of stock in the quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $136.4 million, up 48% YoY, up 8% QoQ; infrastructure approximately $47 million, up 76% YoY; non-GAAP gross margin 59.6%

quarterly_data.signal: First 2026 optical guide. CEO: 'Based on this improved visibility, we expect Keystone to generate about $100 million to $130 million in revenue in '26 with potential upside along with a further step function increase in run rate as we move into 2027.' (In Q&A he referred to it as 'We were guiding to $110 million to $130 million'.) CFO did not break out 2025 optical DSP revenue but noted '3 years ago, we were doing less than $20 million of revenue', and said the ramp 'will be very strong right out of the gate in Q1 and Q2' with 'a few customers that are ramping right now', then grows through the year as new programs come on and share gains build. The CEO said new design wins entering production position MaxLinear 'to grow faster in '26 than we did in '25'; the CFO declined to guide the full year but said he is 'confident that we can outgrow the industry in 2026'.
quarterly_data.figure: Keystone 2026 revenue about $100 million to $130 million

quarterly_data.signal: The Keystone PAM4 DSP family 'is now ramping at major hyperscale data centers in both the U.S. and Asia, supporting 400-gig and 800-gig deployments, both for scale-up and scale-out applications', with additional customer ramps expected throughout the year; MaxLinear is 'in the initial phases of the ramp of our 800-gig product solution'. CEO: 'this year, we could do anywhere between 4 million to 6 million units of PAM4 transceivers'. Scale-up shipments have started but are 'a smaller portion of the revenue', with most in scale-out networks. On position: 'we can safely claim with the top 3 deployers of PAM4 DSP', though in the U.S. 'we got late as the #3' and 'incumbency has incredible value'; he said MaxLinear has strengthened its relative position in 800 gig and that on 1.6 terabit 'our position is strengthening'. He rejected the idea that it is winning on price: 'I don't think in this market, you win by pricing'.
quarterly_data.figure: 4 million to 6 million units of PAM4 transceivers in 2026; top 3 PAM4 DSP deployer

quarterly_data.signal: Rushmore, 'our next-generation family of PAM4 TIAs and 200-gig per lane DSPs targeting 1.6 terabit interconnects', is described as foundational for LRO, electrical retimers, AECs, LPOs and co-packaged optics; 'customer engagement for Rushmore is accelerating faster than expected' and 'We expect Rushmore production revenue ramp starting at the end of 2026', with a strong showing expected at OFC in March. CEO: 'we will really start pulling our weight as 1.6 terabit rolls out', and beyond that a 400 gigabit per lane product will build on the company's low-power implementation capabilities.
quarterly_data.figure: Rushmore production revenue ramp starting at the end of 2026

quarterly_data.signal: CEO's architecture view: 'The market as a whole is still a pluggable market, which is growing very, very fast'; LPO deployments are 'very nichey right now', with limited deployments potentially in 800 gig 'but less so on 1.6 terabits'; LROs have 'got some traction' and are a natural DSP derivative MaxLinear will pursue ('in a short while, we'll have something to show'); CPO 'still is early innings', with a silicon play in which MaxLinear expects to be a player; in scale-up, electrical retimers will be 'a huge volume', and 'At the OFC, we will be announcing our electrical retimers for the Ethernet product category.' Derivative product offerings are planned over 'the next 12 months'.

CFO: backlog and visibility are 'in a much better position', particularly on the optical side, where 'we've got 28-week lead times' and first-half backlog is already in place, with the company pushing for upside. On supply: 'certainly, there's supply chain tightness out there. We're not concerned about that', citing work with suppliers and improvements so far; '80-plus percent of our business is really not exposed to that tightness', while the optical side 'certainly is'. The CFO also flagged 'headwinds with cost increases' on gross margin.
quarterly_data.figure: 28-week lead times; 80-plus percent of business not exposed to supply tightness

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 guidance: revenue between $130 million and $140 million, with growth from infrastructure but seasonal declines in broadband, connectivity and industrial multi-market; GAAP gross margin approximately 56% to 59% and non-GAAP gross margin in the range of 58% and 61% (59.5% at the midpoint). CFO expects mix to shift toward higher-margin infrastructure products and to exit the year with gross margin 'starting with a 6% versus a 5%', despite cost-increase headwinds; OpEx growth 'maybe it's in the 4% to 5% increase this year'. Broadband is expected to be down for 2026 (seasonally soft first half ahead of a DOCSIS 4 upgrade cycle starting at the end of 2026), while connectivity grows on Wi-Fi 7 and 2.5 gig Ethernet.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 revenue $130 million and $140 million; non-GAAP gross margin 58% and 61%

quarterly_data.signal: The Panther hardware storage accelerator SoC family continues to gain design-win traction with Tier 1 network appliance and cloud service providers, helped by 'storage and hybrid memory constraints for AI scale-up and compute'. In Q3/Q4 MaxLinear started sampling Panther 5 'to leading customers and our partners, including Advanced Micro Devices or AMD'; Panther 5 delivers 450 gigabits per second throughput and PCIe Gen 5 connectivity. CEO: 'we expect strong accelerator revenue to at least double in 2026 versus 2025 and potentially again in 2027.'
quarterly_data.figure: Panther 5: 450 gigabits per second throughput; accelerator revenue to at least double in 2026 versus 2025
